opennyai_summary.facts:
The Special Land Acquisition Officer has determined the compensation at Rs.1,200/- per acre and the same was questioned by the claimants Dhulappa S/O Ramanna vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184156644/
16 before
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred the appeals before the Principal District Judge at Gulbarga in various land acquisition claim appeals and the First Appellate Court
by judgment and award dated 29.01.2002, enhanced the compensation to Rs.11,500/- per acre in respect of the acquired lands with all the additional benefits including the interest on additional market value and interest on solatium at the rate of 9% per annum.
Ultimately, these awards made by the Reference Court were questioned before the First Appellate Court and the First Appellate Court, by the impugned judgment and award, enhanced the compensation to Rs.11,500/- per acre,
however on careful perusal of the judgment rendered by this Court in MSA No.580/2010 and MSA No.541/2011, wherein, in identical circumstances and in respect of the very same notification, this Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.35,750/- per acre with all consequential benefits.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not in dispute that the lands in question are acquired for the purpose of construction of lower mullamari project and in this regard, preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was published on 17.06.1976 and the SLAO has awarded compensation of Rs.1,200/-
The said aspect has not been countered by the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In that view of the matter, these appeals are allowed in terms of the judgment and award passed by this Court in MSA No.541/2011.
The appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,750/- per acre with all consequential benefits.
